beat_hypotheses.hypothesis: Because GEODE's declared-relation ledger is EAVT (the house's own row-level, content-addressed relation shape per the org-layering law's EAVT custody section), every relation the house asserts is a separately addressable row carrying its own provenance, so the house can answer 'which constituting act asserted this exact relation, from which source document' for any single edge by walking one ledger row, under an assay that reads query_l_space_sparql_bgp for one edge and its evidence field -- while a plain Protege/Jena/GraphDB triple store cannot answer that without added named-graph or reification bookkeeping most deployments skip, without contradicting the fact that a bare RDF triple carries no provenance slot of its own.
beat_hypotheses.demonstrated_evidence: lib/emsenn/services/561-group/services/science-services-section/sites/l-space.561.group/src/release-graph-artifact.mjs confirms each edge the site's release graph emits carries an `evidence` object (kind, weight, reason) alongside its source/target, sourced from GEODE's ledger via @red-cup-engineering/geode's readDeclaredRelationLedger.
beat_hypotheses.unverified_this_session: the content-addressed (kind:ni digest) EAVT row shape itself is asserted by house doctrine (.claude/rules/org-layering.md, EAVT custody section) and was not independently re-derived from @red-cup-engineering/geode's own source in this session -- that package's internals were not read.

beat_hypotheses.hypothesis: Because the founder's four-regime typing (once encoded) would give every ontology class a proved settling regime rather than a free-text rdfs:comment, the house could answer 'is this concept's status settled, and under which regime' as a typed query the way Protege/Jena cannot, since their OWL classes carry no regime-typed settlement field at all -- while a class with no assigned regime would contradict the encoding being complete.
